historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah The name Ehtiram carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ehtiram was a title given to Ibn Az-Zubair during the First Fitnah (civil war) between Ali ibn Abi Talib and Muawiya I. Ibn Az-Zubair was a major opponent of Muawiya and refused to pledge allegiance to him. Muawiya offered Ibn Az-Zubair the title of Ehtiram and the governorship of Kufa if he would submit. Ibn Az-Zubair rejected the offer and continued his opposition, leading to the Battle of Jamal in 650 CE. Ibn Az-Zubair was defeated and later killed in 661 CE.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's History of Damascus The name Ehtiram carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: During the Ayyubid period, the title Ehtiram was given to the Mamluk Sultans as a sign of respect and reverence. The title was first given to Sultan Qansuh Al-Ghuri in 1468 CE and continued to be used by subsequent Mamluk Sultans until the Ottoman conquest of Egypt in 1517 CE.
